name: Jairus
overview: Jairus is a male synagogue official noted in the Gospel of Mark. He is recognized primarily for his role in seeking Jesus' help to heal his daughter. Scripture highlights his position within the Jewish religious community and his faith in Jesus' power to heal.
namesAndTitles: The name Jairus means 'he gives light,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew name. This proper name does not appear to be given directly by God but is recorded in Mark 5:22.
familyAndRelationships: Jairus is identified as the father of a girl named Talitha, as inferred from Mark 5:23. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional family details.
scriptureSignificance: Jairus is significant in the biblical narrative as a man of religious standing who demonstrates faith in Jesus by appealing for his daughter's healing. His story underscores Jesus' authority over sickness and death, illustrating the compassionate power of Christ. Jairus' interaction with Jesus serves as a powerful example of trust and divine intervention.
